name: cmp
description: Compare two files byte by byte
porting_notes: Four-file port (cmp.c, regular.c, special.c, misc.c). Uses mmap emulation via posix-emu for file-mapped comparison on the regular code path. Exit codes mapped to AmigaDOS conventions: RC=0 (identical), RC=10 (differ or error). Memory-checker audit: CLEAN -- no leaks, argv expansion uses atexit cleanup. Perf-optimizer: c_special loop noted as LOW priority optimisation opportunity.
known_limitations: mmap emulation via posix-emu uses in-memory copy rather than true memory-mapped I/O; performance on very large files may be slower than native. AmigaDOS has no /dev/null equivalent so stdin-only comparisons must use the - argument with a redirected file.
readme:
Short:        Compare two files byte by byte
Type:         util/cli

cmp - Compare two files byte by byte

Original author: UC Berkeley
Source: OpenBSD cmp v1.19

Ported by Duncan Bowring using amiport (AI-assisted porting toolkit).
Project: https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc for AmigaOS 3.x (68000+).
Tested in FS-UAE with AmigaOS 3.1.

Usage:
  cmp [-l | -s] file1 file2 [skip1 [skip2]]

Options:
  -l   Print byte number and values of each difference
  -s   Silent (only return exit status)

Exit Status:
  0    Files are identical
  10   Files differ or an error occurred

Includes full source code (original OpenBSD and ported Amiga versions)
and PORT.md documenting every transformation applied.
